author: Codex
original_finding:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Delete failed private-key outputs**

If writing or syncing the restored key fails—for example because the filesystem runs out of space or `fsyncSync` reports an I/O error—the shared `write()` helper has already created the destination and never unlinks it. The CLI then exits with “No key was accepted,” although a partial or even complete private key may remain, and a retry is blocked because the destination now exists. Remove the newly created file when the write or sync fails, or publish it atomically only after a successful sync.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
repair: Shared CLI output is written and fsynced to an owner-only temporary file before atomic no-overwrite hard-link publication. Write/sync/close/link failures remove failed output; cleanup failure is explicitly surfaced. Initial key creation and restoration share the repaired publisher.
io_refusals: initial key writer sync failure and retry
prior_cross_platform_boundary: Earlier cross-platform proof transferred an encrypted synthetic backup and a public key; private_key_not_copied_from_mac means no plaintext private PEM transfer, not that an encrypted key copy stayed on one device.
